- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoots in the immediate aftermath of sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–8% to align with historical mean reversion tendency.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage upward momentum; increase final 5–7 days of forecast by 2–5% if sentiment remains positive and price is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., alternating +0.30/-0.30), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; adjust forecast to follow sentiment direction with 1–2 day delay.
